new_information: Google won a bankruptcy auction to acquire Spirit Airlines' internal business data for $10 million, outbidding Mercor which bid $7.5 million.
The dataset includes 100 million emails across 80,000 accounts, 500 million Teams messages, 17,082,644 OneDrive files, 20,577,677 SharePoint files, and 667,563 IT tickets.
The dataset contains operational data covering more than 763,000 flights, five million crew pairings, over 1.2 million fuel slips, and records describing the purchase of 787,452 parts.
All data records must be anonymized by a third party before transfer to Google, and Google is barred from attempting to de-anonymize the data.
Passenger and frequent flyer data are explicitly excluded from the data acquired by Google, and Google confirmed it is not purchasing customer data or credit card information.
The transaction remains subject to approval by a US bankruptcy judge, with a court hearing scheduled for 19 August in the US Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of New York.

a netjets cessna citation longitude made an emergency landing at akron-canton airport (cak) in ohio on august 18, 2026, after its nose landing gear failed to extend.

the aircraft n803qs was operating as netjets flight eja803 from washington dulles international airport (iad) to akron-canton.
the aircraft touched down on its main landing gear before the pilots held the nose off the runway, after which the nose settled onto the pavement, sustaining damage to its nose and underside.
the faa registry identifies n803qs as a 2020 textron aviation model 700 citation longitude.
the two pilots on board exited without injury and no passengers were aboard.
